passage: In the colony sandpit, Ojas digs his own road right beside Rehana's castle, never touching it. He doesn't look at her, but he stays. "The blue bus goes from the market to the beach," he says, "and it has two doors, and the back door squeaks." Then he names every stop, in order, twice. Rehana pats sand onto her tower and listens. When her castle is done, Ojas quietly drives his toy bus right up to its gate and parks it there. "Bus stop," he says. Rehana grins. "Okay. My castle has a bus stop now."

qa.q: Where does Ojas park his toy bus?
qa.a: Right up to the gate of Rehana's castle.

qa.q: How does Ojas seem to feel about Rehana when he parks the bus at her castle?
qa.a: He seems friendly and eager to share his favourite thing with her, parking the bus at her gate even though he never looks at her.

qa.q: Which choice by Rehana kept the play going?
qa.a: She kept listening to the bus stops instead of walking off, and she welcomed the bus stop into her castle.

qa.q: How might Rehana see Ojas's play after the bus stop moment?
qa.a: She may realise he was playing with her all along, just side by side instead of face to face.

grounding: It shows a child who plays beside another child and talks at length about a favourite subject, and whose way of connecting is real.

passage: "Ammi, first teeth, then milk, then blue socks." "Shalini, today milk first. The van comes early." "No. Teeth first. Teeth, milk, socks." Her hands flap near her ears. Rehana kneels. "Okay, beta. Show me the chart." Shalini runs to the fridge and taps the picture cards. "Teeth. Milk. Socks. Shoes. Van." "Teeth it is. Super-fast teeth?" "Super-fast teeth." She brushes, gulps the milk, pulls on the socks. At the gate she tugs Rehana's sleeve. "Ammi, tomorrow is Saturday. Saturday chart is different. Saturday has park." "I know. You remind me." "I always remind you." She presses her cheek against Rehana's arm, once, then climbs into the van.

qa.q: What is the order on Shalini's morning chart?
Why does Shalini flap her hands when Rehana says milk first?
qa.a: The change to her set order upsets her; she needs the morning to go in the order she knows.

qa.q: What turning point in the morning made things go smoothly?
qa.a: Rehana asked to see the chart and followed it, making it a game with super-fast teeth instead of arguing.

qa.q: What would change if Rehana had insisted on milk first?
qa.a: Shalini would likely have become more upset, and they might have missed the van and the cheek-press goodbye.

grounding: It shows a child who needs a set order for the day and connects with her mother in her own real way.
